title: Action log — Usability Evaluation Report (Version 1)
feature: Action log tab of a meeting (Version 1)
method: Synthetic Persona Usability Study | NN/G Methodology | 4 Personas | 11 User Stories | 1 Variant
disclaimer: All results come from simulated think-aloud sessions with synthetic personas about the current prototype. Numbers are simulated, not measured user data, and must be validated with real users.
context: Prototype at localhost:5173/action-log.html (Version 1) with seed data: 5 meetings, 22 actions, 11 users. The simulation covers desktop (1280, with and without the drawer), iPad landscape (1024), iPad portrait (800) and phone (390). Source: Figma Meetings › Action log (33037:404462), adapted to the Tasks and Reports responsive patterns.

variants.name: Version 1
variants.summary: Action log tab of a meeting: toolbar (Status and Assignee multi-filters, Clear filters, Export CSV) over a table grouped by meeting (chevron + name + count, expand-all in the header). Columns Status · Assignee · Due date collapse by pane width (Due <960px, Assignee <800px); on phone (<480px) rows become a list with 'status • assignee' under the title and the filters fold into a Filters button + modal. A row opens a detail drawer (inline ≥1024px, overlay below): per-assignee completion toggles, Choose user, due date, linked to, description, attachments, Complete and Delete.

goals.text: Assess scanability: can each persona see which actions are late, whose they are and which meeting they belong to.
Evaluate filtering, clearing and export on desktop and touch.
Check the detail drawer: reading, marking done, assigning and deleting.
Check the responsive behaviour: columns collapsing by pane width, and the phone list.
Quantify simulated task success and SEQ per user story and persona.

stories.text: As a reader, I want to see which actions are overdue at a glance.
As a reader, I want to filter the log by status.
As a reader, I want to filter the log by assignee to see my own actions.
As a reader, I want to open an action and read its details.
As an assignee, I want to mark my part of an action as done.
As a secretary, I want to add another assignee to an action.
As a reader, I want to expand or collapse meetings to find an older action.
As a secretary, I want to export the visible actions.
As a reader, I want to use the log on a phone without losing status or owner.
As a secretary, I want to delete a wrong action without losing others by mistake.
As a reader, I want to clear filters and get back to the full list.

personas.name: Margaret Chen
personas.goal: Before the meeting, see what is overdue and chase owners; export the list for the pack.
personas.mentalModel: Spreadsheet-like tables, filters and CSV export; keyboard first.
personas.risk: Impatient with extra clicks; skims past icon-only controls.

personas.name: David Okafor
personas.goal: Record who owns each action from the last meeting and tick off what is done.
personas.mentalModel: Task lists with explicit buttons and labels.
personas.risk: Hovers every icon; hesitates before destructive actions.
personas.emotion: Careful; worried about changing the wrong item.

personas.name: Patricia Reyes
personas.goal: Find the actions assigned to her and see which are late.
personas.mentalModel: Email and paper lists; reads words, not icons.
personas.risk: Gives up when a control has no label; avoids dense tables.

personas.name: Robert Hale
personas.goal: Glance at open actions on iPad and phone, open one to read details.
personas.mentalModel: Touch lists; tap a row to open it.
personas.risk: No hover, so tooltips are invisible; narrow screens hide columns.

MC.scenario: Scans the list for red items before the call.
MC.behaviour: Spots the red due dates and Overdue badges in one pass.
MC.friction: Overdue is shown by badge and red date; colour is backed by a label.

MC.scenario: Filters to Overdue and Pending review.
MC.behaviour: Opens the Status dropdown, ticks two values.
MC.friction: The control then reads '2 selected', so the chosen values are not visible without reopening it.

MC.scenario: Looks for an action from an older meeting.
MC.behaviour: Uses the expand-all icon in the header.
MC.friction: Icon-only; she finds it because the tooltip appears on hover.

MC.scenario: Exports the filtered list for the pack.
MC.friction: No confirmation, so it is unclear whether the filters were applied to the file.

MC.behaviour: Opens the row, clicks the trash icon in the drawer footer.
MC.friction: Deletes immediately with no confirmation or undo.

MC.behaviour: Uses Clear filters next to the toolbar.
MC.friction: None; the first two meetings reopen, which she expects.

DO.scenario: Opens the Deed of Variation action.
DO.behaviour: Clicks the row; the drawer opens on the right.
DO.friction: The table narrows when the drawer opens, so Assignee is hidden at 1280px.

DO.behaviour: Hovers the circle beside the name for a tooltip, then clicks it.
DO.friction: The toggle is an icon only; 'Completed 1/4' is the only text feedback.

DO.behaviour: Finds 'Choose user' under the people list and picks a name.
DO.friction: The field reads as a placeholder, not as a button.

DO.behaviour: Opens Assignee and scrolls a long list of 11 names.
DO.friction: The dropdown has no search; the control then reads '1 selected'.

DO.behaviour: Reaches for the trash icon, hesitates, closes the drawer.
DO.friction: No confirmation, so he does not risk it.

DO.behaviour: Reads Status badges row by row.
DO.friction: Statuses and dates are equally weighted, so overdue does not stand out from a distance.

PR.behaviour: Does not notice the Assignee filter at first, then opens it.
PR.friction: Both filters read 'All statuses / All assignees'; she expects a Search box.

PR.behaviour: Reads Overdue badges but ignores the red date.
Clicks the chevron on a group row.
PR.friction: Three meetings are all called 'Board of Directors / February 2026', so she cannot tell them apart.

PR.scenario: Opens an action to read it.
PR.behaviour: Clicks the title; the drawer opens.
PR.friction: Description is empty for most actions, so the drawer shows little beyond status and people.

PR.scenario: Looks for a way to export.
PR.behaviour: Finds Export (a labelled button at desktop width).
Looks for a reset and finds Clear filters.
PR.friction: The button only appears after a filter is set.

DIR.behaviour: Reads rows as a list with status and owner under the title.
DIR.friction: Due date is not shown on a phone row; he opens the row to see it.

DIR.scenario: Filters by status on iPad portrait (800px).
DIR.behaviour: Taps Filters, picks a status in the modal, taps Done.
DIR.friction: Assignee is hidden in the table at this width, so the owner cannot be seen after filtering.

DIR.scenario: Opens an action on iPad landscape.
DIR.behaviour: Taps the row; the drawer opens beside the table.
DIR.friction: The drawer is 360px at 1024px; long titles wrap over several lines.

DIR.behaviour: Taps the circle beside his name.
DIR.friction: The target is 32px, below the 44px touch minimum.
None; the whole row is the target.

DIR.behaviour: Taps the trash icon in the drawer footer.

shared: Delete has no confirmation or undo: David hesitates and avoids it, Robert has no confirmation sheet on phone.
Selected filter values and the icon-only expand-all / mark-done controls depend on hover or reopening the dropdown; touch readers cannot use tooltips.
Meeting names repeat ('Board of Directors / February 2026' ×3), so readers cannot tell groups apart without opening them.
When the pane narrows (iPad, drawer open) the owner disappears from the table.

divergent.MC: Fast; reopens a dropdown to check '2 selected'
divergent.PR: Does not notice the filters at first
divergent.DIR: Uses the Filters button + modal on phone and iPad portrait
Taps the row; drawer overlays on phone
Taps the trash on phone; no confirmation

heuristics.name: Visibility of system status
heuristics.evidence: Overdue is badge + red date and 'Completed N/M' tracks assignees; but Export gives no confirmation and filter values read '2 selected'.

heuristics.name: Match with the real world
heuristics.evidence: 'Linked to' and 'Pending review' are clear; three meetings share the title 'Board of Directors / February 2026'.

heuristics.name: User control and freedom
heuristics.evidence: Delete is immediate with no confirmation or undo, on desktop and phone.

heuristics.name: Consistency and standards
heuristics.evidence: One pattern: row opens the drawer; DS Dropdown, Button, Tooltip, StickyFooter throughout.

heuristics.name: Error prevention
heuristics.evidence: Delete without confirmation; a Complete button next to Delete.

heuristics.name: Recognition rather than recall
heuristics.evidence: Expand-all and mark-done are icon-only and need a tooltip; selected filter values are hidden behind '2 selected'.

heuristics.name: Flexibility and efficiency
heuristics.evidence: Filters, expand-all and CSV export help power users; no search, sorting or bulk actions.

heuristics.name: Aesthetic and minimalist design
heuristics.evidence: Three columns, calm table, details moved into the drawer.

heuristics.name: Help users recover from errors
heuristics.evidence: Clear filters resets; there is no undo for delete.

heuristics.name: Accessibility
heuristics.evidence: Labels on icon buttons, tooltips and focus rings; touch targets 32px, Assignee/Due hidden below 800/960px.

issues.issue: Delete has no confirmation or undo (drawer footer, desktop and phone)
issues.impact: David avoids deleting; Margaret removes a duplicate she cannot restore

issues.issue: Three meetings share one name, 'Board of Directors / February 2026', so groups cannot be told apart
issues.impact: Patricia and Robert expand the wrong meeting

issues.issue: Assignee column is hidden below 800px and Due date below 960px; the drawer narrows the table further
issues.impact: Owner is lost after filtering on iPad and beside the drawer

issues.issue: Selected filter values read '2 selected', not the names
issues.impact: Margaret and David reopen the dropdown to check

issues.issue: Expand-all and Mark-as-done are icon-only; tooltips need hover
issues.impact: David hovers each icon; touch users do not see tooltips

issues.issue: Export has no confirmation and its scope (filtered or all) is not stated
issues.impact: Margaret is unsure the filters were applied

recommendations.title: Confirm before deleting and offer Undo
recommendations.fix: Show a confirmation modal (a bottom sheet on phone) naming the action, or delete with a Toast that has Undo.

recommendations.title: Give meetings a date and a distinct title
recommendations.fix: Show the meeting date in the group row ('Feb 12, 2026') and sort groups by date.

recommendations.title: Keep the owner visible when columns collapse
recommendations.fix: Show 'status • assignee' under the title below 800px, as on phone, instead of hiding Assignee entirely.

recommendations.title: Show selected filters as chips or names
recommendations.fix: Replace '2 selected' with the value names (truncate with +N) or chips under the toolbar.

recommendations.title: Label the expand-all and mark-done controls on touch
recommendations.fix: Keep the tooltip on hover and add a persistent text label or aria-visible state on touch.

phases.name: Phase 1 — Fix the blockers
phases.text: Apply R1–R3, then re-run the same six tasks per persona.

phases.name: Phase 2 — Touch
phases.text: Test iPad portrait and phone with real directors; check the 44px touch minimum for mark-done.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Real users
phases.text: 2 real users per persona type, including 2 directors on iPad.

questions: Do readers expect to find their own actions through a filter, a search box, or a 'My actions' view?
Is the date of the meeting enough to tell groups apart, or do they need the agenda item too?
Should the Complete button sit beside Delete in the drawer footer?

takeaways: The Action log reads well on desktop: scanning, filtering and opening an action succeed for most personas.
The biggest risk is deleting without confirmation; it is also the lowest-effort fix.
Repeated meeting names and the vanishing Assignee column make the list harder to read on iPad.
Validate with real directors; every score here is simulated.

strengths.label: STRENGTH
strengths.text: Overdue is shown by a badge and a red date, so colour is never the only signal (US01 SEQ 6–7).

strengths.label: STRENGTH
strengths.text: On phone the table becomes a list with status and owner under the title, and the filters fold into one Filters button.
